claims.text: Atomic-size mismatches in HfNbTaTiZr produce local lattice distortions.
Local lattice distortions promote short-range atomic ordering in HfNbTaTiZr.
Short-range ordering suppresses anharmonic lattice vibrations.
Suppression of anharmonic lattice vibrations reduces the rate of thermal expansion.
Suppression of anharmonic lattice vibrations mitigates elastic softening at elevated temperatures.
The arc-melted and homogenized initial HfNbTaTiZr alloy is single phase.
An additional moderate-temperature anneal below recrystallization will enhance short-range ordering.
The additional anneal can enhance short-range ordering without changing the overall single-phase microstructure.
The post-processing thermal treatment enhances both local lattice distortions and short-range atomic order.
Increased short-range ordering stiffens the lattice by reducing anharmonic atomic vibrations.
The annealed alloy will have a lower thermal expansion coefficient than the baseline alloy at elevated temperatures.
The annealed alloy will retain higher elastic moduli than the baseline alloy at elevated temperatures.
The annealed alloy will show less temperature-induced softening in its stress–strain response than the baseline alloy.
The proposed mechanism should remain operative from room temperature to approximately 1000°C.
HfNbTaTiZr remains below its melting point and free of phase instability throughout the proposed range up to approximately 1000°C.

contradictions.description: The comparator is called an 'as-cast material' in the hypothesis, but elsewhere it is described as arc-melted and homogenized. Homogenization is a post-casting treatment, so the exact baseline state is ambiguous.
